title: Dogs with Extraordinary Jobs
description: Looking at how a Sprocker spaniel's sense of smell and the protective instincts of an Anatolian shepherd dog are playing a vital role in the conservation of endangered species. Plus, a couple of canine colleagues who protect aircraft from potentially dangerous bird strikes during take-off and landing. Using their natural speed, stamina and desire to chase, the pair works at King Shaka Airport in Durban, South Africa, responding to emergency call-outs from air-traffic control.

title: Reef Wrecks
description: An exploration of shipwrecks and the ecosystems they support, beginning with those located off the coast of Bonaire, an island in the Caribbean.

title: Animals Like Us
description: The frigate bird likes to steal meals of food from smaller birds. The warthog enjoys a spa day, while the African elephant sends secret messages.

title: Aussie Snake Wranglers: Deadly Pursuit
description: Stu and Liv catch a pregnant red-bellied black snake at a busy resort, while Mick and Adele face a lace monitor lizard.

title: Aussie Snake Wranglers: Deadly Pursuit
description: Stu and Liv outwit a blue tongue lizard, Jess and Dan free a trapped snake, and Mick and Adele rush a python rescue fast.

title: Great Lakes Wild
description: A research team travels to the uninhabited island of Isle Royale in Lake Superior, which has been a battleground between moose and wolves since the early 20th century.

title: Great Lakes Wild
description: The invasive Asian carp, which have destroyed native fish populations - and their food supplies - throughout America's waterways.

title: Planet Weird
description: The world's most incredible wild creatures, revealing their strange behaviours and peculiar survival techniques. This edition uncovers nature's strangest courtship rituals, where clever tricks, unlikely alliances and fierce rivalries all play a part in finding a mate.

title: Big Cats, Nine Lives
description: Documentary series following lions, leopards and tigers through the defining stages of their lives, from vulnerable cubhood to power conflicts, reproduction and decline.

title: Wildlife ER
description: Documentary following the work of dedicated staff at the RSPCA Hospital in Brisbane, Australia.

title: Big Cats: An Amazing Animal Family
description: Part one of two. Biologist Patrick Aryee explores how cats have evolved throughout the millennia, learning to thrive in inhospitable environments, as well as becoming the world's most popular pet. In the first edition there is spectacular footage of caracals jumping three metres to catch flying birds, and a rare Bornean bay cat, which was thought to have been extinct. Patrick finds out how tigers made the transition from South-east Asia's steamy jungles to the -40C temperatures of Siberia, and m

title: Big Cats: An Amazing Animal Family
description: Patrick Aryee concludes his two-part exploration of the feline family tree, revealing how the Canadian lynx learned to thrive in the snow and spread out, evolving and inhabiting new parts of the Americas. In Belize, he mounts an experiment that showcases the margay's supersharp senses and gravity-defying acrobatics, and heads to the training track with a cheetah to find out what speed it is capable of. Finally, Patrick tells the story of the cat's domestication in Essaouira, Morocco, believed to

title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
description: David Attenborough employs the latest technologies to explore the violence, rivalries and deadly weaponry existing within the world of bugs. This first episode examines the survival tactics of its terrifying residents including killer ants, trap-setting spiders and beetles with the ability to shoot boiling chemicals at their enemies.

title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
description: The broadcaster continues his bug-eyed view of the world of creepy-crawlies, revealing how predators defuse the defences of their prey. Highlights include the cockroach wasp, busy preparing a tasty - and very live - treat for its young, the whirligig beetle, which employs a water-based radar system, and the jumping portia spider, which feeds on other arachnids.

title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
description: A further selection of creepy-crawly close-ups, focusing on courtship in the bug world. Highlights include scorpions shaking their booty, the perfume-wearing nasonia wasp and the tropical cricket, for whom romance goes out of the window as it uses bribery to seal the deal with would-be partners. One potential partner to steer well clear of, however, is the praying mantis, the female of which is notorious for eating the male just after - or even during - mating. Narrated by David Attenborough.

title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
description: A close-up view of sex, bug-style, as David Attenborough talks viewers through the different ways in which creepy-crawlies reproduce. Size matters for the minuscule male orb spider, creepily sneaking up on its intended and trying to mate without her noticing, while there's no rest for the lothario-like butterfly, which has plenty of notches on its proverbial bedpost. However, the harvestman spider has no use for sex at all, and reproduces by cloning itself.

title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
description: David Attenborough shifts the focus to bugs that prefer co-operation rather than conflict. They include burrowing cockroaches, the suitably named social spiders - which share a 30-metre web - the queen bee and her happy hive of workers and green ants pulling together to build a nest.

title: Micro Monsters with David Attenborough
description: The broadcaster concludes his close-up examination of the creepy-crawly world, shifting focus to the bugs' ultimate invention - the colony. Key residents of these minuscule mega-cities include honey bees, termites, leafcutter ants - who have a knack for farming - and their Argentine cousins, members of a community so vast it spans an entire continent.

title: Deadly Australians
description: As water flows from Australia's highlands into the seas, environmental changes set the stage for unexpected clashes between predators and their prey.

title: Shark Squad
description: Leading shark ecologist Mauricio Hoyos attempts a TV first as he attaches a camera to the dorsal fin of a great white shark off Guadalupe Island.

title: Wild Philippines
description: Discovering a world shaped by fire and water, as cameras capture Philippine eagles soaring above ancient forests and rare crocodiles lurking below the river's surface.

title: Wild Philippines
description: Cameras follow turtles and tiger sharks roaming volcanic reefs, and tarsiers leaping through forests on the hunt.

title: Deadly Australians
description: As water flows from Australia's highlands into the seas, environmental changes set the stage for unexpected clashes between predators and their prey.

title: Shark Squad
description: Leading shark ecologist Mauricio Hoyos attempts a TV first as he attaches a camera to the dorsal fin of a great white shark off Guadalupe Island.

title: America's Wild Border: Northern Exposure
description: The animals that live on the border between the US and Canada face many challenges - even politics. This documentary reveals how the boundary affects them over 12 months.

title: Uptown Otters
description: Following families of otters in Singapore, beginning with the Bay clan's lush territory, where matriarch Anna offers lavish feasts, but faces internal dissent.

title: Uptown Otters
description: Anna spends quality time with the young pups, then visit a flooded mangrove before checking in on the Townies, whose resources are thinning.

title: Aussie Snake Wranglers: Deadly Pursuit
description: Stu and Liv catch a pregnant red-bellied black snake at a busy resort, while Mick and Adele face a lace monitor lizard.

title: Aussie Snake Wranglers: Deadly Pursuit
description: Stu and Liv outwit a blue tongue lizard, Jess and Dan free a trapped snake, and Mick and Adele rush a python rescue fast.

title: Extraordinary Animals
description: Aggressive behaviour is not limited to the most obvious culprits. Revealing how koalas, cockatoos, clownfish and more can exhibit surprising behaviours in order to survive.

title: Extraordinary Animals
description: How animals employ extravagant behaviours to entice mates or warn off predators, proving that standing out can be the ultimate survival strategy.

title: City Wildlife Rescue
description: The search begins for a Cooper's hawk who's taken a dangerous dip in a backyard pool. Plus, the centre's skunks try to avoid getting their shots.

title: City Wildlife Rescue
description: When a baby mink is abandoned in a store, the team gets to work on some behavioural training. But will this sweet little one be tough enough for the wild when they're done?

title: Nature's Dress Code: Who Wears What and Why?
description: Every living creature, from the amoeba to the blue whale, needs a suitable coat. Dive deep into the fashion styles of the natural world with this colourful documentary.

title: Humanlike: The Chimps of Fongoli
description: Documentary about a group of elusive chimpanzees living in the Fongoli region of Senegal, on the southern edge of the Sahara Desert. It's the hottest, driest place in the world that chimps can live and they really shouldn't be here - so how do they survive?

title: David Attenborough's Kingdom of Plants
description: The naturalist and film-maker explores the many varieties of plant life housed at the Royal Botanic Gardens in Kew, west London, and explains what they reveal about the natural world and the development of life on Earth. He begins inside the establishment's Palm House, whose climate has been engineered to simulate conditions found in rainforests, charting the evolution of plants that grow in the world's wettest regions and investigating how flowering plants spread across the globe so rapidly.

title: David Attenborough's Kingdom of Plants
description: The naturalist explores how the plants at Kew Gardens change through the seasons and demonstrates the surprising properties of several species, including the predatory pond-dwelling bladderwort utricularia and a fungus that appears to be capable of mind control. He also discusses the largest single organism on the planet, visits the world's biggest flower and explains how plants and insects can communicate using scents and music.

title: David Attenborough's Kingdom of Plants
description: The naturalist concludes his exploration of the Royal Botanic Gardens in Kew, west London, by examining plants that have evolved to minimise their dependence on water, enabling them to survive in the world's driest environments. He witnesses a cactus blooming at midnight, tells the story of the spectacular flowering of the Agave franzosinii, and visits the Millennium Seed Bank, a facility designed to save plants from future extinction.

title: Secrets of the Enchanted Waters
description: A journey through mystical lakes, where life adapts, survives and transforms, while witnessing the power of ancient beasts like the snapping turtle and walking tall with flamingos.

title: Evolution Earth
description: Scientists discover animals with the power to restore our grasslands, turning them into carbon sinks that could slow climate change.

title: Big Cat Country
description: The lionesses from the Hollywood pride are in grave trouble, with intruders occupying their prime hunting grounds and the four dangerous Nomad lions blocking their path home.

title: Big Cat Country
description: The MK pride faces its toughest moment yet as their matriarch and best hunter Surabi's life hangs in the balance after being gored by a buffalo.

title: Planet Weird
description: Cameras journey with nature's nomads and hitchhikers, from monarch butterflies on an epic migration to the hidden world within a sloth's fur.

title: Big Cats, Nine Lives
description: Following a tiger from tiny cub to formidable hunter, as instinct and stealth guide it through a solitary world of shifting territories, fierce rivalry and ever-present danger.

title: David Attenborough's Dragons and Damsels
description: Arguably more beautiful than butterflies, better fliers than hummingbirds and with intriguing and complex behavioural patterns - dragonflies and damselflies are marvels of the insect kingdom. This documentary uses the latest camera technology to show their manoeuvres, mating strategies, territorial behaviour and flight dynamics, revealing them to be the ultimate insect.

title: Jellyfish: The Ocean's New Rulers
description: Investigating the growing population of jellyfish blooms around the world and examining whether this species is on its way to dominating the oceans as they once did.

title: David Attenborough Meets Obama
description: Another chance to see Barack Obama's conversation, recorded in May 2015, with renowned naturalist and film-maker David Attenborough. In a twist on usual convention, the then-US president took the role of interviewer, quizzing Attenborough about his thoughts on the future of the planet, their shared passion for nature, and potential ways to protect the environment.
